updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - September 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for September 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Your Distribution

In August, the fund received $6,729 from Rush Creek, reflecting June oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3, the NE Newby Unit 27-7, the Newby 27-8, and the Newby 27-9 (the first revenue for the 27-9). That income (less fund expenses and a small operating reserve) was distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure.

This distribution was processed on August 17, totaling $312 per $100,000 invested.

One item of note: payment for the RCR Newby 27-7's June oil sales was held up by a paperwork error on the oil purchaser's side. The issue has been resolved, and that revenue will be included in Rush Creek's September payment to the fund – and therefore in the next distribution.

Updates from the Field – August 2026

Buxton 1: Completion Underway, with Early Signs of Oil

Completion work at the Buxton field is in motion. In late August, Rush Creek perforated and acid-treated the lower Viola zone on the Buxton 1 and began swabbing the well to recover reservoir fluids. The early results are encouraging: the first swab runs have brought up good-looking oil with almost no water.

The Viola wasn't the original target zone for this field, and the deeper Wilcox zones remain the primary target. But completing it first was a deliberate decision by Rush Creek to accelerate oil production, and therefore cash flow.

The Viola doesn't appear to need water-disposal infrastructure, which means it can produce now, while the dedicated water-injection well that the deeper zones require is still waiting on a drilling rig. Once the injection well is drilled, Rush Creek will complete the Wilcox zones and commingle production from both.

If the swab results hold, Rush Creek will equip the well with a pumping unit and bring it into production from the Viola zone. The workover rig then moves to the Buxton 2 to begin the same completion work there.

Buxton Field Infrastructure Is In

While completion timing at the Buxton field has moved slower than any of us wanted, important groundwork has been laid:

  • All roadways to the well sites are built and complete.
  • All tank pads are built, with production tanks ordered and awaiting delivery.
  • Primary electrical power is connected.
  • The infrastructure to move produced crude off-site is in place.
  • The dedicated workover rig we reported last month is now owned outright by Rush Creek and is stationed at the field full-time.

The remaining piece is the dedicated water-injection well, which will be drilled when the drilling rig arrives on location – the drilling rig contractor has the Buxton field next in line as it finishes its current job.

RCR Newby 34-2: OCC Approval Received

In late August, the Oklahoma Corporation Commission issued its final approval of the injection well that serves the Newby 34 section. (Rush Creek's tracer survey required one amended submission, which was approved within about a week.)

With the paperwork done, the remaining work is physical and small: roughly 330 feet of electrical line to power the injection well, which Rush Creek's crew is installing now. The 34-2 itself can run on a gas engine ahead of the field's grid power arriving (more on that below) – if it runs well that way, production could begin in September. If the well ends up needing the electrical line to run reliably, startup will take a few weeks longer.

Newby 34-5: Frac Back on the Schedule

The 34-5's frac had been on hold pending the injection-well approval covered above. With that approval in hand, Rush Creek is getting back on its frac contractor's schedule – the current estimate is roughly two weeks out, though summer demand means exact dates firm up on short notice. The well is otherwise ready to go: drilled and cased, with facilities and pumpjack already installed.

Newby 34-4: Gas Test Delivers

The 34-4's gas test came back in late August with excellent results. The gas quality is high, and Enerfin Resources, the gas gathering company, has confirmed it will accept the well's gas. Rush Creek believes the 34-4 will be a strong commercial gas well – strong enough that its gas revenue may rival its oil revenue.

The tie-in is also simpler than expected, and will not require complicated compression equipment. Rush Creek is running its portion of the line now, and the current estimate for completing the tie-in is two to three weeks.

Encouragingly, fluid began migrating into the wellbore during the gas test – an early sign of the oil to come once the well's gas cap is drawn down.

Newby Field: The Buildout Continues

Infrastructure work is moving on the Newby side as well:

  • The water-injection system for the Newby 34 section is essentially complete – water transfer lines are already installed, and with the OCC approval in hand, the injection well needs only its short electrical run to start service.
  • Rush Creek is running overhead grid power across the entire field, from section 27 through section 34, over the next few weeks. That puts the 34-2, 34-4, and 34-5 on dependable electric service rather than gas engines.
  • The gas line being run for the 34-4 gives the field gas takeaway for the long term: any of the fund's Newby wells that encounter significant gas will be able to tie in, rather than sitting shut in behind a gas cap the way the 34-4 has been.

Medicine Crow 33-1: Evaluating Completion Results

After perforating and acid-treating the Medicine Crow in early August, the well's response so far has been below what Rush Creek hoped to see. Rush Creek is bringing in an independent third-party petroleum engineer to evaluate the well's data, and plans a second acid treatment to rule out the possibility that the first treatment was compromised, before deciding next steps for the well. We expect to have more to report next month.

Well-by-Well Status

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 – Producing
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 – Producing
    • Newby 27-8 – Producing
    • Newby 27-9 – Producing
    • RCR Newby 27-7 – Producing
  • Ready for Production
    • RCR Newby 34-2 – OCC approval received; electrical hookup in progress
    • Newby 34-4 – gas-line tie-in underway
  • Completion In Progress
    • Buxton 1 – Viola zone perforated and acidized; swabbing with early oil shows
    • Buxton 2 – next in line; the workover rig moves over once Buxton 1's completion wraps
    • Newby 34-5 – frac being scheduled (~2 weeks estimated)
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 – evaluating initial completion results; second acid treatment planned

Financials & Production Overview

The figures below reflect June 2026 production across the fund's producing wells.

As a reminder, the fund receives payment from Rush Creek two months in arrears of production, and we report production data in the update period in which the corresponding payment is received.

June was the fund's biggest sales month to date. The producing wells sold a combined 1,440 barrels of oil – 474 barrels from the RCR Newby 34-3, 319 barrels from the NE Newby Unit 27-7, 333 barrels from the Newby 27-8, 152 barrels from the Newby 27-9, and 162 barrels from the RCR Newby 27-7 – with the 27-9 and RCR 27-7 both recording their first oil sales. That's a 75% increase over May's volume, with five wells now selling oil.

The oil sold at an average of ~$78 per barrel in June, a discount of ~8% to the $85 average WTI price for the month, and still well above the $60 per barrel price we used in the fund's initial underwriting. Oil prices pulled back meaningfully from their spring highs in June (WTI averaged $102 in May), which tempered the revenue impact of the higher sales volume.

Note: the most recent months are preliminary and subject to revision as final expense billing is received.

Thank you for your continued confidence in us. If you have any questions about your investment or the fund as a whole, please reach out anytime.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - August 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for August 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Your Distribution

The fund's first investor distribution was processed on July 28.

You should have received an automated notification from the investor portal reflecting your specific amount (please let us know if this did not come through). Note that distributions are delivered by ACH to the bank account on file in your investor portal, and it typically takes 3-5 business days for the funds to arrive in your account.

In July, the fund received $6,959 from Rush Creek, reflecting May oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3, the NE Newby Unit 27-7, and the Newby 27-8. With the fund's origination fee fully recovered, that income (less fund expenses and a small operating reserve) was distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure. This first distribution equals $304 per $100,000 invested.

Although a modest amount, this is the milestone we've been working toward since the first well came online in November, and we're excited to have the fund's cash flow now reaching investors. As the remaining six wells come online and production ramps, we expect these distributions to grow accordingly.

Going forward, we will process investor distributions monthly following receipt of Rush Creek's payment to the fund.

Updates from the Field – July 2026

Checking In on the Wells in Person

In mid-July, Dustin and I spent two days in Tulsa with the Rush Creek team, touring some of the fund's well sites and seeing production operations up close. It was a great visit, and we appreciated the time Alan and Taylor spent walking us through everything, including new drilling opportunities that will be included in Oil Fund VII (which is open for investment).

Buxton 1 & 2: Power On, Completion Being Scheduled

Primary electrical power is now connected at the Buxton 1 and 2 well sites. Production facilities are scheduled to arrive on site the first week of August, and Rush Creek is moving forward with the acid and perforating work to establish the wells' initial flow rates.

Rather than wait in line for a third-party completion rig (the regional contractor Rush Creek planned to use had a backlog more than a dozen jobs deep), Rush Creek has secured a dedicated workover rig for the Buxton sites under a master services agreement – meaning the completion work, and everything after it, runs on Rush Creek's schedule rather than a contractor's. A drilling rig is also expected on location within a couple of weeks to drill the dedicated water injection well that will serve the Buxton field.

With power on, facilities arriving, and a dedicated rig on the way, we anticipate the Buxtons will begin production in late August. As always, unforeseen delays in any of these pieces, including severe weather, could push this back.

Medicine Crow 33-1: Completion Underway

Completion work on the Medicine Crow 33-1 began this week. Rush Creek moved a workover rig onto the location, with perforating and an acid treatment scheduled for early August.

Depending on how the well responds to the acid treatment, it may not need a frac at all to begin producing – Rush Creek noted it could behave like the RCR Newby 34-3 and RCR Newby 27-7, both of which came online flowing on natural pressure. The flow test will tell us much more, and production facilities are already ordered. We currently anticipate production to begin by September.

RCR Newby 34-2 & Newby 34-5: Waiting on One OCC Approval

Both of these wells are ready to go and waiting on a single regulatory approval: the final Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC) sign-off on the injection well that serves the Newby 34 section.

As reported last month, Rush Creek completed the required tracer survey and installed the required pressure-monitoring system weeks ago; the delay is on the OCC's side, where the staff member reviewing the file left their position and the file was reassigned to a new reviewer who is being brought up to speed. Rush Creek is escalating directly – its attorneys, its geologist, and Alan personally are working the file with senior OCC staff to get it across the line.

The delay has had real consequences: the 34-5's frac was scheduled for July 29 and had to be called off because the injection well (which handles the frac's water disposal) still lacks this final approval, and the 34-2 remains shut in awaiting the same sign-off. Once the approval lands, Rush Creek can turn the 34-2 on and frac the 34-5 in short order.

We are hopeful that this will finally be resolved in the coming weeks, which would allow both wells to begin production in August.

Newby 34-4: Gas Tie-In Pending

The 34-4 remains shut in, waiting on the gas gathering company (Interfin Resources) to approve a tie-in to its line. As discussed in last month's update, the well's substantial gas cap has to be drawn off through that line before the oil can flow freely, so nothing can be produced until the tie-in is complete.

Rush Creek is pressing the issue up Interfin's chain of command, but heavy rains across the region in June created a backlog of utility and pipeline work that has slowed everyone down. We don't have a firm timeline to report – but the expectation is that once the gas line tie-in occurs, the pressure will be relieved quickly, oil will begin to flow, and the 34-4 will produce income from the sale of both oil and gas.

Well-by-Well Status

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 – Producing
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 – Producing
    • Newby 27-8 – Producing
    • Newby 27-9 – Producing
    • RCR Newby 27-7 – Producing
  • Ready for Production
    • RCR Newby 34-2 – awaiting final OCC approval of the injection well
    • Newby 34-4 – awaiting the gas-line tie-in
  • Completion In Progress
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 – Workover rig on location; perforating and acid treatment in progress
    • Newby 34-5 – Drilled and cased with facilities and pumpjack installed; frac pending the injection-well approval
    • Buxton 1 – Primary power on; facilities arriving; completion being scheduled
    • Buxton 2 – Same status as Buxton 1

Financials & Production Overview

The figures below reflect May 2026 production across the fund's producing wells.

As a reminder, the fund receives payment from Rush Creek two months in arrears of production, and we report production data in the update period in which the corresponding payment is received.

In May, the fund's producing wells sold a combined 822 barrels of oil – 501 barrels from the RCR Newby 34-3, 161 barrels from the NE Newby Unit 27-7, and 160 barrels from the Newby 27-8, the first oil sales for that well.

The oil sold at an average of ~$95 per barrel in May, a discount of ~7% to the $102 average WTI price for the month, and well above the $60 per barrel price we used in the fund's initial underwriting.

Note: the most recent months are preliminary and subject to revision as final expense billing is received.

Thank you for your continued confidence in us. If you have any questions about your investment or the fund as a whole, please reach out anytime.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - July 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for July 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Join us in Tulsa – July 14 & 15

Dustin and I will be in Tulsa, OK on July 14 & 15 to meet with the Rush Creek management team and visit some of our well sites.

We'll spend part of the day on the 14th in the oil field visiting the active well sites, followed by dinner that evening with Alan Girardot and Taylor Rogers (Rush Creek's CEO and CIO).

One investor is already planning to join us, and we'd love to have more. If you'd like to come along and see your investment in person, just reply and let us know so we can send you the details.

Your Distribution

In June, the fund received $12,136 from Rush Creek, reflecting April oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3 and the NE Newby Unit 27-7.

The fund's 3% origination fee has now been fully recovered from early production revenue. With that complete, all subsequent income (less fund expenses and reserves) will be distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure.

We expect the first investor distribution to be made in mid-to-late July, once we receive payment from Rush Creek for May's production. When that distribution is processed, you'll receive an automated notification from the investor portal.

This is a good moment to log in and confirm the bank account on file is the one you'd like your distributions deposited into. If you have any questions or issues updating it, just reach out and we'll help you make any changes.

Updates from the Field – June 2026

June was a wet month in Oklahoma. Repeated heavy downpours and flash flooding washed out roads and well-site access paths on several occasions, which pushed some completion work later than planned.

Buxton 1 & 2: Electrical and Injection Infrastructure

Both the Buxton 1 and Buxton 2 remain drilled, cased, and ready for final completion activities. Rush Creek has completed its own portion of the site's electrical build-out (the private and secondary overhead lines), and is now waiting on the local utility to bring primary power and install transformers. The wells' flow rates can be established with a workover rig independent of utility power, and Rush Creek hopes to do so as soon as the site dries out and becomes accessible by the rig.

Production from the Buxtons is still targeted for the end of July, alongside the drilling of a dedicated injection well to serve them (the injection well's surface damages have been negotiated and the well has been permitted).

RCR Newby 27-7: New Producer Online

The RCR Newby 27-7 came online in early June and has been producing a steady 20-25 BPD. Notably, the well began flowing on an acid treatment alone, without a frac. Rush Creek believes it tapped into a natural fracture network and, similar to the Newby 34-3, plans to let the well run on this natural pressure, only fracking when production levels begin to drop. The well experienced a brief 48-hour pause after coming online to swap a faulty pump unit under warranty, but is back online and producing consistently.

Newby 34-4: A Gas and Oil Well

The Newby 34-4 came online in late May and in early June encountered a substantial natural gas cap. The quantity of gas is more than can be safely vented and the quality is sufficient to sell commercially, so Rush Creek is arranging to tie into a nearby gas gathering line. Once that gas is drawn off the wellbore, the liquid oil is expected to flow in more freely – a timeframe expected within days of relieving the well's gas pressure. The gas tie-in is a relatively minor piece of work, and final gas testing is imminent.

While this was unexpected, it means that the 34-4 will be a long-term gas and oil well, with the gas revenue likely to cover a substantial part of the well's operating costs.

RCR Newby 34-2: Injection Well Nearing Approval

The RCR Newby 34-2 has been drilled and ready to produce since late December, held up by a state-level injection-well exception from the Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC). Rush Creek completed the required tracer survey (which confirmed the injected water stays in the target zone, the key concern) and has installed a state-required monitoring system. With everything now submitted to the OCC and a final state inspection expected to occur once the site dries out and is accessible, Rush Creek expects production to begin in July.

Medicine Crow 33-1: Awaiting Completion

The Medicine Crow 33-1, drilled to TD in late May with the strong Prue-sand geology we reported last month, has now had its pooling order approved. Completion work was delayed by weather and rig scheduling and is expected to follow once Rush Creek's rig frees up.

Newby 34-5: Awaiting Facilities

The Newby 34-5 is drilled and cased, with facilities and a frac standing by, ready to go. The hold-up has been access – the location sits next to a creek that flooded repeatedly this month. Rush Creek expects to move facilities in and complete the well once the site dries out, likely bringing it online around mid-July.

Well-by-Well Status

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 – Producing (25-30 BPD)
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 – Producing (~8-10 BPD)
    • Newby 27-8 – Producing (~20 BPD)
    • Newby 27-9 – Producing (~8-10 BPD)
    • Newby 34-4 – Producing gas; oil expected to follow the gas-line tie-in (see above)
    • RCR Newby 27-7 – Producing (20-25 BPD)
  • Completion In Progress
    • RCR Newby 34-2 – Injection-well compliance complete; final OCC inspection pending; production imminent
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 – Drilled to TD with strong geology; pooling order approved; completion to follow
    • Newby 34-5 – Drilled and cased; awaiting facilities and frac (weather-delayed)
    • Buxton 1 – Drilled and cased; Rush Creek's electrical build-out done; awaiting utility power and a dedicated injection well
    • Buxton 2 – Same status as Buxton 1

Financials & Production Overview

The figures below reflect April 2026 production across the fund's producing wells.

As a reminder, the fund receives payment from Rush Creek two months in arrears of production, and we report production data in the update period in which the corresponding payment is received. Accordingly, May's production data will appear in the August 1 update.

In April, the fund's producing wells sold a combined 1,284 barrels of oil – 806.79 barrels from the RCR Newby 34-3 and 477.19 barrels from the NE Newby Unit 27-7.

The oil sold at an average of $94.85 per barrel in April, a discount of ~5.5% to the $100.32 average WTI price for the month, and well above the $60 per barrel price we used in the fund's initial underwriting.

Beginning with this update, we're also reporting the fund's net income from oil sales – its share of oil sales after production taxes and lease operating expenses. The two charts below show it for the month overall and broken out by well:

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - June 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for June 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Your Distribution

In April, the fund received $5,015.03 from Rush Creek, reflecting March oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3 and the NE Newby Unit 27-7.

The fund's early production revenue has continued to be applied toward the 3% origination fee, as described in prior updates. As of this update, $40,300 of the $52,950 origination fee has been recovered, leaving $12,650 remaining. It's worth noting that essentially all of this revenue has come from a single producing well – the RCR Newby 34-3, which has been online and selling oil since November.

Once the origination fee is fully recovered, all subsequent income will be distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure. With multiple new wells having come online in May and very little of the fee left to recover, we expect to clear it shortly – initial investor distributions are expected to begin August 1.

Updates from the Field – May 2026

Two New Wells Online & Selling Oil

Both the Newby 27-8 and Newby 27-9 were fracked at the end of April and came online in mid-May.

The Newby 27-8 came online at an initial production (IP) rate of ~55 barrels per day and has since settled into a steady rate in the 25-30 BPD range. The Newby 27-9 had IP of ~20 BPD and is has stabilized around 10 BPD – a rate consistent with the typical profile for Newby wells. Both wells have already had their first pickups of oil sales.

RCR Newby 34-2: Injection-Well Permit Cleared

The RCR Newby 34-2 has been drilled and ready to produce since late December, but full production required a state-level injection-well exception from the Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC). After an extended review, that exception was approved, with Rush Creek now completing the final compliance steps (a tracer survey and a tubing-pressure monitoring system) before turning the well on. They now expect the 34-2 to enter full production by July.

Newby 34-4: Online After Skinner Completion

As described last month, Rush Creek pivoted the Newby 34-4 to the Skinner sand after the Dutcher zone proved difficult. The well was fracked in early May, perforated, and began pumping in late May, throwing back significant fluid and gas as it cleans up (encouraging early signs). We'll report production rates as the well stabilizes.

Medicine Crow 33-1: Drilled with Standout Geology

Drilling on the Medicine Crow 33-1 reached total depth in late May, with strong results in the target zone. The well's objective was the Prue sand, with the location designed to intersect a clean, oil-filled sand channel.

Rush Creek's consulting geologist, Kim Drew, reported 34 feet of clean pay sand in the Prue, with log values well within productive parameters. From his drilling report (emphasis ours):

These samples were the best Prue sand samples I have ever seen. The sample bag had a very strong oil odor before I even opened it… I have never seen these kinds of oil shows in a Prue sand before.

His overall conclusion was that the well found “a very nice oil field” in the targeted channel. Completion work is expected to follow as production facilities become available, potentially by the end of June.

RCR Newby 27-7: Promising Early Flows

The RCR Newby 27-7 was acidized in May with good oil shows, and by late May the surface tanks, rods, and tubing had been set, with the well already attempting to flow under its own natural pressure ahead of pump-jack installation. Early flowback has been strong (~70 barrels per day) which is an encouraging initial indicator. It's still too early to know where the well will settle once it's fully equipped and producing steadily, but an initial flowback rate this high is a good sign. The pump jack is expected to be delivered and installed in early June, bringing this well online.

Buxton 1 & 2: Power Infrastructure Going In

Both Buxton 1 and Buxton 2 remain drilled, cased, and ready, awaiting primary electrical service before they can be completed and begin production. Primary power was approved in late April, and by late May the local cooperative had run electric lines and poles to both wells. With the remaining engineering install, completion work, and construction of a dedicated injection well sized for the field, Rush Creek now anticipates production from the Buxtons beginning around early July.

Newby 34-5: Awaiting Facilities

The Newby 34-5 is drilled and cased, awaiting tank facilities before it can be perforated and completed. Rush Creek expects to move on the completion as soon as tanks arrive – potentially as early as June.

Well-by-Well Status Updates

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 – Producing (25-30 BPD)
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 – Producing (~10 BPD)
    • Newby 27-8 – Producing (see update above)
    • Newby 27-9 – Producing (see update above)
    • Newby 34-4 – Began production in late May (see update above)
  • Completion In Progress
    • RCR Newby 34-2 – Completed and ready; injection-well exception approved; final compliance steps underway
    • RCR Newby 27-7 – Acidized with good shows; tanks, rods, and tubing set; awaiting pump-jack installation
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 – Drilled to TD with great geology; cased; completion to follow facilities installation
    • Newby 34-5 – Drilled and cased; awaiting facilities and completion
    • Buxton 1 – Drilled and cased; electric lines and poles run; awaiting power install and dedicated injection well
    • Buxton 2 – Same status as Buxton 1

Financials & Production Overview

The figures below reflect March 2026 production across the fund's producing wells.

As a reminder, the fund receives payment from Rush Creek two months in arrears of production, and we report production data in the update period in which the corresponding payment is received. Accordingly, April's production data will appear in the July 1 update.

In March, the fund's producing wells sold a combined 838 barrels of oil – 670.84 barrels from the RCR Newby 34-3 and 167.56 barrels from the NE Newby Unit 27-7 – generating gross revenue of approximately $74,178.

The oil sold at an average of $88.48 per barrel in March, a discount of ~3% to the $91.38 average WTI price for the month, and well above the $60 per barrel price we used in the fund's initial underwriting.

Thank you for your continued confidence in us. If you have any questions about your investment or the fund as a whole, please reach out anytime.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - May 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for May 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

K-1 Timing

As a final reminder, your 2025 Schedule K-1 is now available on your investor portal account (uploaded on March 23).

If you're having trouble accessing your K-1 or have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Your Distribution

We continue to anticipate that investor distributions will begin in Q2 at the earliest.

In April, the fund received $6,176.01 from Rush Creek, reflecting February oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3. This brings the total payments received by the fund to approximately $26,400 to date. The lower amount versus the prior month's payment reflects reduced February production, which was impacted by a paraffin restriction in the well's flow line – see the operational update below for further detail.

As permitted under the Private Placement Memorandum, the Managing General Partner can take a 3% origination fee based on total capital raised ($52,950 on a $1.765M total raise). Rather than deducting this fee from investor capital at closing, we elected to take it from the fund's initial production revenue. Early cash flow will continue to be applied toward this fee before investor distributions begin. Once the origination fee has been fully satisfied, all subsequent income will be distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure.

Several wells we previously expected to be producing by now remain in late-stage completion, and we recognize this has continued to push our production timeline beyond what we communicated in prior updates. Going forward, we are providing more conservative timing guidance – describing each well in terms of its current operational stage (drilled & cased, in completion, awaiting facilities, online, etc.) rather than committing to specific production months. Stage-based reporting will give you a clearer picture of where each well actually stands at any point in time, since oil and gas operations are subject to weather, equipment, permitting, and supply chain factors that can shift any individual milestone.

Operational Updates

Amarada Field Drilling Results

Both Amarada wells (Buxton 1 and Buxton 2) were drilled and logged earlier this year and are now in late-stage pre-completion. We've received substantial new information from drilling on both the geological findings and the infrastructure plan.

Both wells confirmed the Wilcox formation as a strong oil-bearing target, consistent with our underwriting going into the field. On Buxton 1, both the 1st and 2nd Wilcox intervals showed productive signatures, with the 2nd Wilcox described by Rush Creek as “very thick with an oil water contact that could yield the same volumes of oil production without the associated water production of the 1st Wilcox.” Buxton 2 confirmed the field extends west, with the 1st Wilcox showing even better oil signatures than Buxton 1.

Beyond the Wilcox, Buxton 1 also intersected the Viola formation which Rush Creek's CEO Alan Girardot called “the best log on a Viola well I have seen in my tenure in the oil and gas business.”

Most significantly, Buxton 1 encountered an unexpected zone called the Lower Calvin at approximately 2,600 feet that Rush Creek described as a “new field discovery:”

Most surprising and what I am excited about was the discovery of the Lower Calvin, which appears to be a high porosity, low cost completion, oil saturated zone that on paper appears to be a new field discovery which could eclipse 100,000 bbls of oil per wellbore at a relatively shallow depth and little to no associated water production.

The Lower Calvin was not part of our original underwriting on the Amarada wells – it's upside that materializes when the wells are completed and tested. Rush Creek's plan is to develop the deeper Wilcox first, with the Lower Calvin available as a low-cost shallow completion to be brought online when economics support it.

These results came in materially larger than the field was originally underwritten for. As a result, Rush Creek has decided to drill a brand-new, dedicated injection well sized for the field's full development potential rather than retrofitting an older, smaller wellbore for a larger purpose.

Separately, primary electrical service to the field was approved on April 29 by the local electrical cooperative – a meaningful step forward after several months of waiting; engineering and installation are estimated at approximately two weeks from approval.

Production from Buxton 1 and Buxton 2 is now expected in late summer, accounting for primary power installation, completion activities, and dedicated injection well construction. This is later than we previously communicated, but the resulting infrastructure positions the field for sustained development across multiple additional wells in the Amarada area.

RCR Newby 34-3: Continued Paraffin Management

The 34-3's February production was reduced versus prior months due to a continued paraffin buildup in the flow line – the same issue described in the April 1 update.

Rush Creek attempted to schedule hot oilers in April to clear the line but was unable to get equipment to the site due to muddy conditions following severe weather. Hot oiling will proceed as soon as the location dries out.

The well itself continues to perform; the production drop is a flow-line restriction, not a well or reservoir issue.

Newby 27-8 and 27-9: Successfully Fracked

The last week of April marked the most active completion period the fund has had to date.

The Newby 27-8 was successfully fracked on April 30; immediately following, the Rush Creek crew rigged up at the Newby 27-9 to begin its frac on the same day. Both wells will have completion rigs moved over the hole in the coming days, with first oil sales expected in May.

Newby 34-4: Pivoting to the Skinner Sand

Last month we reported that the Newby 34-4 was undergoing a second acid treatment in the Dutcher zone. After reviewing the results and weighing the risks of fracking the Dutcher (which carried some risk of impacting nearby production from the 34-3), Rush Creek decided to pivot to the Skinner zone.

During the initial Skinner acid clean-up, the well recorded a shut-in pressure of 920 PSI – described by Rush Creek's consulting geologist Kim Drew as “the highest pressure I have ever seen or heard of in the Skinner sand” and a strong indicator that the Skinner reservoir has significant gas drive (natural pressure capable of pushing oil to surface without artificial lift).

The Skinner frac is now scheduled for Monday, May 4. Production facilities are already in place, so the well can be brought online quickly once fracked.

This 34-4 pressure has also informed the geological outlook on the Newby 34-5. Drew's drilling report on the 34-5 cites the same Skinner interval as the primary target, with strong oil indicators in the rock samples and excellent log values – “the high pressures seen in the nearby wells indicate that this well has virgin pressure and it should be a very good producer.” The 34-5 is currently awaiting completion; the location remains too muddy from severe weather for a completion rig to access.

RCR Newby 27-7: Active Two-Zone Completion Attempt

The RCR Newby 27-7 (a separate well from the producing NE Newby Unit 27-7) was drilled and cased earlier this year. Its primary Skinner target was perforated earlier in April, and on April 30 Rush Creek also perforated the deeper Cromwell sand zone to test it as a potential additional producing interval.

Acid is scheduled to arrive in early May, after which Rush Creek will swab and test the Cromwell to determine whether it can produce in commercial volumes. If the Cromwell is productive, the well will have multiple producing zones – meaningful additional upside on this wellbore. If not, Rush Creek will proceed with the Skinner as the primary producing zone.

Well-by-Well Status Updates

Per the timing-language guidance above, this section now describes each well in terms of its current operational stage rather than committing to specific production dates.

  • Online & Producing

  • Completion In Progress

    • Newby 27-8 - Fracked April 30; completion rig moving in
    • Newby 27-9 - Fracked April 30; completion rig moving in
    • Newby 34-4 - Skinner frac scheduled May 4; production facilities in place
    • Newby 34-5 - Drilled and cased to the Skinner; awaiting completion rig and facilities
    • RCR Newby 34-2 - Completed and ready for production; awaiting state-level injection-well exception or completion of dedicated new injection well, whichever resolves first
    • Buxton 1 (formerly Amarada East #1) - Drilled and cased; primary power approved April 29; awaiting dedicated new injection well (see above)
    • Buxton 2 (formerly Amarada West #1) - Same status as Buxton 1
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 - Drilling completion hampered by equipment failures and severe weather; completion expected imminently

Financials & Production Overview

Our oil purchaser (MV Purchasing) is currently transitioning to a new back-office system and is behind in delivering detailed run statements showing per-well barrel volumes and prices. Cash flow has not been affected – Rush Creek has confirmed they have received payment for March production on schedule, and we expect the fund's corresponding payment to be received in mid-May.

Going forward, production data will appear in the same monthly update period in which the fund receives the corresponding payment: a two-month-arrears reporting cadence consistent with payment timing. March production data will be reported in the June 1 update.

In the meantime, Rush Creek's daily monitoring confirms that both producing wells continued to perform in line with prior trends through March: the NE Newby Unit 27-7 at approximately 20 barrels per day, and the RCR Newby 34-3 at approximately 25-30 barrels per day between paraffin remediation cycles.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - April 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for April 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

K-1 Timing

2025 Schedule K-1s were uploaded to your investor portal account on March 23.

If you have any questions about your K-1 or are having trouble accessing it in the portal, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Your Distribution

We continue to anticipate that investor distributions will begin in Q2 at the earliest.

In March, the fund received $8,019.59 from Rush Creek, reflecting January oil sales from the RCR Newby 34-3. This brings the total payments received by the fund to approximately $20,300 to date.

As permitted under the Private Placement Memorandum, the Managing General Partner can take a 3% origination fee based on total capital raised ($52,950 on a $1.765M total raise). Rather than deducting this fee from investor capital at closing, we elected to take it from the fund's initial production revenue. Early cash flow will continue to be applied toward this fee before investor distributions begin. Once the origination fee has been fully satisfied, all subsequent income will be distributed to investors according to the fund's 80/20 waterfall structure.

While we made meaningful progress in March and now have two wells online and producing, several wells that were expected to be producing by now have been delayed by facility and equipment delivery timelines, permitting, and completion sequencing. We are pushing Rush Creek hard on these items and anticipate meaningful acceleration in April as facilities are delivered and additional wells come online. That said, we recognize this is taking longer than what we indicated in prior updates and appreciate your patience.

Oil Prices

As you're likely aware, WTI crude oil is currently trading above $100 per barrel.

We originally underwrote this fund with a baseline oil price assumption of $60 per barrel. Nobody can predict how long prices will stay at these elevated levels, but the current environment is materially favorable for the fund. Sustained higher prices shorten the timeline for recovery of invested capital and increase the potential returns on every barrel produced.

Rush Creek is working aggressively to bring wells online as quickly as possible to take advantage of this pricing window, including using temporary storage tanks where needed rather than waiting on permanent facilities.

Operational Updates

RCR Newby 34-3: Steady Production, Brief Flow Line Issue

The RCR Newby 34-3 sold 687.84 barrels of oil in February. This was down from prior months due to a paraffin buildup in the flow line (the pipeline connecting the well to the storage tanks). Paraffin naturally occurs in crude oil and can gradually accumulate inside pipelines, restricting the flow of oil over time. This is a known and common occurrence in these types of wells, not an indication of any issue with the well or the reservoir itself.

Rush Creek proactively injects mineral spirits into the line alongside the oil to help slow this buildup (the beige barrels in the photo below), but periodically the accumulation reaches a point where the line needs to be cleared. When that happens, hot oil is run through the line to melt the paraffin and restore full flow. Rush Creek identified the restriction, cleared the line, and production returned to its prior level immediately.

Rush Creek actively monitors production levels daily, and when paraffin buildup begins to impact flow, they address it quickly.

NE Newby Unit 27-7: Online and Producing

The NE Newby Unit 27-7 came online in early March with initial production (IP) of approximately 25 barrels of oil per day. This is a strong initial rate, and we'll continue to report on production as data becomes available. The well has already generated its first oil sales.

This brings the fund's producing well count to two, with several more expected to follow in the coming weeks.

RCR Newby 27-7: Drilled with Excellent Geological Results

The RCR Newby 27-7 (a separate well from the NE Newby Unit 27-7 above) was drilled in March and showed very promising results.

Here is an excerpt from the drilling report issued by Rush Creek's consulting geologist on the primary target zone (emphasis ours):

These were some of the best [Skinner sand] samples I have seen in a long time. Some of the samples showed the sand to be very clean, well rounded quartz grains with good visible porosity and permeability… I noted a good oil sheen in the wash bucket and a strong oil odor. I set the wash bucket in my kitchen sink and the entire room smelled like crude oil.

In plain terms: the rock samples pulled from this well during drilling showed clear, strong indicators of oil – visible to the eye and by smell. The well's electrical log readings, which help measure the likelihood of oil versus water in the formation, were the highest recorded in this field to date. The geologist's overall assessment: "The Skinner [sand] is an absolutely gorgeous zone that will be a good producer."

Beyond the primary target, the geologist also identified two additional deeper zones in the well that show potential to produce oil. These secondary zones would need to be tested separately, but their presence adds further potential upside to an already encouraging well.

The well is currently awaiting production facilities (tanks and separation equipment). Rush Creek has ordered the necessary equipment and expects to have it on site within the next 30 days. Production is anticipated by mid-May.

Well-by-Well Status Updates

Here is the current status of each well in the portfolio:

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 - Producing (see update above)
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 - Producing (see update above)
  • In Progress
    • RCR Newby 27-7 - Drilled with excellent geological results (see update above). Awaiting facility delivery. Fracking planned for early April. Production expected mid-May
    • Newby 27-8 - Drilled, perforated, and swabbed with strong oil shows. Awaiting facility delivery to schedule fracking. Production expected mid-to-late May
    • Newby 27-9 - Drilled, swabbed, and acidized. Same as 27-8: awaiting facility delivery for fracking. Production expected mid-to-late May
    • Newby 34-4 - Undergoing additional completion work. An initial acid treatment did not reach the target zone as intended, so the well was reperforated and a second acid treatment is being performed with a modified approach to direct the treatment into the correct zone. If the acid job is successful, the well will come online. If not, a small hydraulic fracture will be performed. Production expected mid-to-late April
    • RCR Newby 34-2 - Completed and ready for production, but requires an injection well permit (or a granted exception) to begin. This permit is pending with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. We expect a decision by mid-April at the latest, after which production can begin promptly
    • Buxton 1 (formerly Amarada East #1) - Drilled and cased. Perforations scheduled for early April. Awaiting electrical infrastructure (expected late April). Production expected late May
    • Buxton 2 (formerly Amarada West #1) - Same status as Buxton 1. Production expected late May
  • Scheduled
    • Newby 34-5 - Drilling permit received. Location build-out underway and drilling expected to begin immediately. Production expected mid-May
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 - Drilling permit expected any day. Equipment staged on site, and drilling expected to begin immediately. Production expected mid-April

Financials & Production Overview

With two wells now producing and several more expected to come online in the coming weeks, this section will expand meaningfully in future updates as production data, revenue, and operating expenses become available across multiple wells.

API numbers are issued when drilling permits are approved. Below is an updated listing of wells in the fund along with API numbers (where available) and the fund's working interest ownership percentage:

Production data continues to be reported in arrears. February's production data (in the RCR Newby 34-3 update above) will be reflected in fund financials in March. March's production data will appear in the May 1 update.

Investor Site Visit Recap

March 13-14 | Tulsa & Creek County, OK

On March 13 and 14, we traveled to Oklahoma to meet with the Rush Creek Resources team and visit some of our wells in Oil Fund VI. Several investors joined us for the trip, which included dinner with Rush Creek's CEO Alan Girardot and Chief Investment Officer Taylor Rogers on Friday evening in Tulsa, followed by a full day in the field on Saturday.

Saturday morning we met at Rush Creek's office in Bristow, rearranged into four-wheel-drive vehicles (a necessity for navigating the off-road terrain of the oil field) and headed out to the Newby well sites in Creek County, where the majority of the fund's wells are located.

Over the course of the day, we were able to see operations firsthand across multiple stages of the drilling and completion process:

  • A completion rig actively working on the Newby 27-9
  • The RCR Newby 27-7 in its first hours of drilling - the rig had spudded that morning and was at ~230 feet when we arrived
  • The RCR Newby 34-3 pumping in action - our longest-producing well, where we could see (and smell) the oil firsthand
  • The Newby 34-4 and associated tank batteries nearby
  • A panoramic view of the broader Newby field from an elevated vantage point, where Alan walked us through his development strategy for the area

Key Takeaways

Visible progress. For those of us who visited the area last August, the change was striking. Where there were previously just a handful of well sites, there is now an active, multi-well development with rigs, completion equipment, and tank batteries spread across the field.

No dry holes. Of all the wells drilled to date in this fund, none have come back dry. The geological targets that Rush Creek and their consulting geologist identified have consistently shown oil – a meaningful track record as the program continues.

Production on the wells that are online is solid. Seeing the 34-3 operating in person and hearing Alan discuss its steady, low-cost production reinforced what we've been reporting in these updates. The NE Newby Unit 27-7, which had just come online, was also already producing and selling oil.

The team is growing. Rush Creek is not a large operator, and that's by design – their smaller size allows them to move quickly, make real-time decisions in the field, and adjust plans as conditions evolve. They've also been strengthening their team. We had the chance to meet Julian Schreiber, Rush Creek's new VP of Operations & Exploration. Julian was originally on a path toward diplomatic/intelligence work and Mandarin studies, but after spending a summer as a roughneck he changed his degree to geology and hasn't looked back. He started full-time with Rush Creek earlier this year and has quickly become an integral part of the operation.

Mindful of the price environment. Alan discussed how current oil prices are influencing decisions on the fund's wells specifically. Several of our wells have multiple prospective oil-producing zones at different depths. With prices elevated, Rush Creek plans to test and produce from multiple zones where possible, maximizing near-term revenue. If prices were to decline, they would focus on single-zone production and preserve the deeper reserves for a more favorable price environment – a disciplined approach to managing the long-term resource value of the fund's assets.

Confidence in the operator. Alan also shared his broader development vision for the Newby field that extends well beyond the wells in this fund. While those future plans don't directly impact Fund VI, the depth of geological knowledge, the long-term strategic thinking, and the hands-on operational approach we observed throughout the day gave us added confidence in the team managing our wells.

We came away from the visit encouraged by both the assets and the team operating them. We're grateful to the investors who made the trip, and to Alan and Taylor for their hospitality – which included grilling burgers for the group out at the 27-9 well site.

Thank you for your continued confidence in us. If you have any questions about your investment or the fund as a whole, please reach out anytime.

RCR Newby 34-3: Continued Consistent Production

The RCR Newby 34-3 produced and sold 1,055 barrels of oil in January, averaging approximately 34 barrels per day. The well continues to produce under its own natural pressure and remains choked back to maintain consistent production.

As we've discussed in prior updates, this production rate remains very solid - particularly given that the well has not required hydraulic fracturing (fracking) to stimulate flow.

Amarada Field Discovery – A Major Development

The biggest news this month comes from the Amarada field in Seminole County, where both wells in our program were drilled in February with results that exceeded expectations.

A note on well naming: In prior updates, we referred to these wells as “Amarada East #1” and “Amarada West #1.” These were working names used during the planning phase.

Now that drilling permits have been issued, the formal legal well names are Buxton 1 (formerly Amarada East) and Buxton 2 (formerly Amarada West). We will use the formal names going forward.

Buxton 1 (Amarada East) was drilled to a total depth of 4,300 feet, and the results were described as outstanding. The primary target, the Wilcox formation, was confirmed present with strong indicators of oil. Beyond the Wilcox, drilling also encountered oil in additional zones at shallower depths that were not part of the original target, effectively giving us multiple potential producing formations in a single wellbore. This means the well has multiple opportunities to generate additional revenue beyond the initial targeted zone.

Buxton 2 (Amarada West) was drilled shortly after and confirmed the oil field extends to the west. In some zones, the results looked even better than the Buxton 1. The well also showed signs of a large natural fracture system in one of the deeper formations, a positive indicator that oil can flow freely into the wellbore.

Both Buxton 1 and Buxton 2 are now cased and awaiting completion.

The local electrical cooperative in Seminole County requires approximately 12 weeks to establish primary electrical service to the Amarada field. During this waiting period, Rush Creek plans to conduct flow testing to establish initial production (IP) rate estimates and will be building out the surface infrastructure needed to produce and sell oil from these wells. We currently anticipate production to begin in late May.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - January 2026
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for January 2026, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our eleven-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Fund Oversubscription and Portfolio Expansion

We're excited to report that the fund experienced significantly higher investor demand than originally anticipated, with subscriptions exceeding our initial target by over $300,000.

Rush Creek had additional well inventory available that we were able to add to the fund's drilling program, allowing us to accommodate this increased interest. This required raising the maximum offering size beyond what was stated in the original Private Placement Memorandum.

Legal Notice: For those who have not yet seen it, please review the Supplement to Private Placement Memorandum, which constitutes our formal legal notice of the increased offering amount.

New Wells Added to Portfolio

Of the wells available to add to the fund, one was the Newby 34-5. Here is an excerpt from Rush Creek's consulting geologist's report on the geology of this prospect (emphasis ours):

I am proposing that you drill a well in the E/2 S/2 NE/4 NE/4 of Section 34. This location should be up dip from the Newby #34-3 well [our current strong-performing well] and should be in the heart of the clean, porous, permeable sand channel. I am expecting between twenty and thirty feet of sand in an advantageous structural position. This could be a very big oil and gas producer.
 It should also be noted that although [a competitor's] well was not successful in the Gilcrease they had a Skinner sand that showed fifteen feet of great looking sand with 15 Ohms and 15% porosity. The zone reportedly had 900 PSI the day after they perforated the top five feet of the sand. That is the highest pressure I have ever seen in the Skinner sand. The Newby #34-5 should also be productive in the Skinner sand.

I fully expect the proposed well to be an excellent producer from the Skinner and the Gilcrease sand as well. I am looking forward to drilling and completing the well.

The Newby 34-5 will be added to the fund with a similar working interest percentage as our other Newby 34 wells. We are also adding a smaller working interest ownership in the Newby 27-7. Note that this is a separate well (legally named RCR Newby 27-7) from our existing Newby 27-7 well (legally named NE Newby Unit 27-7).

This brings the total wells in the fund's portfolio from nine to eleven (11).

Your Distribution

In last month's update, we anticipated distributions would begin in March because we expected two to three additional wells to come online and begin producing in December. However, weather complications, permitting delays, and holiday scheduling prevented those wells from coming online as expected.

With drilling and completion activities now progressing through early 2026, we currently anticipate commencing distributions in Q2 at the earliest. We will continue to provide updated timing as operations progress and more wells begin production.

As a reminder, the fund receives payment from the operator two months in arrears. For example, oil sold in February would result in payment to the fund in mid-April, with distributions processed to investors on May 1.

Operational Updates

RCR Newby 34-3: Continued Strong Performance

The Newby 34-3 sold 663 barrels in November, a strong production amount considering the well was only online for approximately one week during that month.

The well continues to experience gas locking consistent with the massive natural pressure in the reservoir. As a remedy, it has been choked back to produce at a lower but more consistent rate. However, the current production rate remains substantial, especially considering the natural flow and lower operating expenses that accompany it.

Rush Creek intends to maintain the current production level until it materially changes. The natural pressure is expected to decline within the next 6-12 months, at which point the well will be hydraulically fractured to re-stimulate production.

Well-by-Well Status Updates

Here is the current status of each well in the portfolio:

  • Online & Producing
    • RCR Newby 34-3 - Producing (see update above)
  • In Progress
    • NE Newby Unit 27-7 - Drilled. Awaiting delivery of site infrastructure (storage tanks) for completion
    • RCR Newby 34-2 - Fracking completed in late December. Production expected to begin in early-mid January
    • Newby 34-4 - Drilling completed in late December, pipe setting in progress.
  • Scheduled
    • Amarada East #1 - Scheduled for drilling mid-January
    • Amarada West #1 - Scheduled for drilling late January
    • Newby 27-8 - Scheduled for drilling early January
    • Newby 27-9 - Scheduled for drilling mid-January
    • Newby 34-5 - Drilling expected to begin in February
    • RCR Newby 27-7 - Drilling expected to begin in February
    • Medicine Crow 33-1 - Scheduled for drilling late January

Financials & Production Overview

With the addition of the Newby 34-5 and Newby 27-7 to the portfolio, here is an updated listing of the wells in the fund, along with the fund's working interest ownership in each:

In December, Rush Creek began onboarding us to their new production data management system, which will allow us to provide detailed well-by-well production data, revenue, and expenses in future updates as wells come online and begin producing.

Production data will continue to be reported in arrears. For example, December's production data will be reflected in February's update, January's data in March's update, and so on.

Note About Oil Prices and 2026 Production

As drilling progresses in early 2026, we want to make you aware of how oil price movements may influence production decisions across the fund's wells.

As a general rule, Rush Creek aims to avoid producing large volumes of oil when prices are significantly depressed. This is especially true in the early stages of a drilling program, when production rates are highest. Selling large amounts of oil at extremely low prices lowers investor returns and extends the timeline to capital recovery.

With this in mind, Rush Creek has informed us that if oil prices decline significantly in 2026, they may take a more conservative production approach across our wells. This would result in lower near-term cash distributions, but would preserve oil reserves to be produced and sold when prices recover, maximizing total returns over the life of the investment.

Conversely, if prices remain stable or increase, production will be optimized to maximize cash flow while market conditions are favorable.

We encourage you to monitor oil prices (WTI specifically) in the coming months. Significant price movements in early-to-mid 2026 may influence production timing and, subsequently, our distribution schedule. Rush Creek will make these decisions with the goal of maximizing total returns rather than following a predetermined production schedule that ignores market conditions.

updates.title: Bidwell Oil Fund VI Update - December 2025
updates.html:
We're pleased to present your monthly investment update for December 2025, reflecting the latest developments regarding production and operations of our nine-well portfolio in Oklahoma.

Your Distribution

A note on distributions while production is still ramping:

The fund receives payment from the operator (Rush Creek) two months in arrears of the month of oil production. For example, for oil sold in December 2025, the fund expects to be paid mid-February 2026. We would then process distributions to investors on March 1.

As we had one well come online during November, and expect two or three more to begin production in December, we currently anticipate commencing distributions by March 2026.

Operational Updates

Newby 34-3: A Rare and Significant Discovery

The Newby 34-3 has proven to be an exceptional well that represents an increasingly rare outcome in modern oil and gas operations. When the well was perforated in mid-November, it began flowing oil naturally up the casing at 100+ barrels per day without any artificial lift or stimulation. Alan Girardot, Rush Creek's CEO said that this is "something [he's] been searching for [his] entire career." Finding reservoir pressure of this magnitude in a pressure-depleted area is highly unusual and consequential.

To put this in perspective: the well has such strong natural pressure that even with flow controls in place to manage production, it continues to produce at high rates. Rush Creek has already picked up three tank loads with a fourth in progress. They are installing additional tank capacity on site – infrastructure they didn't anticipate needing this early in the drilling program.

Understanding the Production Profile

This natural flow is driven by reservoir pressure that will eventually decline, but the timeline is uncertain. Rush Creek's senior advisors have cited historical examples of similar Dutcher sand wells that flowed 100+ barrels per day for an entire year before declining. Once the natural pressure depletes, the well will be hydraulically fractured (fracked), which should result in a second production curve with strong initial rates followed by the longer-term decline we originally modeled.

In essence, the Newby 34-3 may deliver two distinct production phases: the current high-rate natural flow (duration unknown, potentially months to a year), followed by post-stimulation production that should perform in line with or better than our original projections. This represents significant upside that was not built into our initial models.

Operational Impact and Timing

The exceptional performance of the 34-3 has necessitated operational adjustments. Rush Creek has prioritized completing tank facilities, running tubing, and managing the natural flow before moving forward with other planned drilling operations. This is exactly the kind of "good problem" we want to have – delaying planned work because an active well is producing more oil than anticipated and requires infrastructure buildout to handle the volumes.

Competitive Validation and Strategic Response

The success of the Newby 34-3 has attracted immediate competitive attention. A competing operator with extensive seismic data in the area has mobilized a drilling rig to the lease boundary and is currently drilling to access the same reservoir structure. This operator previously drilled a well to the south that came in at 80 barrels per day and has since declined to approximately 30 barrels per day after six months of production – still producing well without stimulation.

The competitor's actions represent powerful third-party validation of the geology. They have invested millions in seismic data, drilled multiple wells (including two dry holes) to map the reservoir, and are now rushing to drill as close to our lease line as legally permissible.

Given that this appears to be a finite oil pool with substantial reserves, Rush Creek determined that protecting our position required immediate action. The fund exercised its rights to participate in a new offset well, the Newby 34-4, which will be drilled between the two proven producers (our 34-3 and the competitor's well).

Drilling on the 34-4 is expected to begin in early December, weather depending.

Remaining Drilling Schedule

Following completion of the Newby 34-4, operations will proceed with the remaining wells in the program:

  • Newby 34-2: Drilled and scheduled for fracking in early-to-mid December.
  • Newby 27-7: Drilled and awaiting completion.
  • Newby 27-8 and 27-9: Rush Creek plans to drill these wells back-to-back immediately after drilling is complete on the 34-4. Additional tank capacity is being delivered in the second week of December to support the 34-2 and 34-4 completions. Given the strong natural flow observed in the 34-3, Rush Creek is prioritizing tank capacity for the 34-4 ahead of other wells to enable immediate production if similar reservoir pressure is encountered.
  • Amarada East & West Wells and Medicine Crow 33-1 - Scheduled for drilling in early-to-mid January.

Completion schedules will be implemented in real time as drilling results develop. We will continue to provide detailed updates as operations progress and formal production data becomes available from Rush Creek beginning later this month.
